findings_to_judge.finding: Q3 FY26 laps the second-weakest lemon price in eight quarters ($17.02/carton in Q3 FY25) while management said on 9 June that realised pricing was already above $20/carton and rising about $1/carton a month, yet the 3-analyst FY26 revenue consensus of $132.13M against $42.1M of actual H1 revenue implies H2 of ~$90.0M versus H2 FY25's $90.3M - i.e. the sell side is modelling H2 flat and giving no credit to either the price comp or the Sunkist volume shift into H2.

The reiterated FY26 guide of 4.0-4.5M fresh lemon cartons is arithmetically stretched: H1 FY26 delivered 681,000 (Q1, $17.41) + 1,028,000 (Q2, $16.63) = 1,709,000 cartons, down ~32% year on year, so the guide requires H2 of 2,291,000-2,791,000 against H2 FY25's 1,397,000 + 821,000 = 2,218,000 - the top end would need a Q4 (Aug-Oct, the seasonal trough) of roughly 1.9M cartons versus 821,000 last year, which the company has never done.

Limoneira's lender deferred the debt service coverage ratio covenant in December 2025 so that it next resumes 'measurement as of October 31, 2026' at 1.25:1.0 - six weeks after the fiscal year the company is now two-thirds through - against H1 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of minus $9.4M (Q1 -$7.7M, Q2 -$1.7M), FY25 full-year adjusted EBITDA of minus $6.452M, total debt of $94,120,000, cash of $891,000 and only $22,096,000 of remaining revolver capacity.

The federal gate for Limoneira's stated FY2026 Colorado River water monetisation opened 19 days before this print: Interior issued the post-2026 Record of Decision on 21 August 2026, ordering 1.25 million acre-feet of annual Lower Basin reductions with Arizona absorbing 760,000 acre-feet - and Limoneira decided in April 2026 to cease citrus farming on its last 600 lemon acres in Yuma specifically 'to monetize Class 3 Colorado River water rights by conserving water', telling investors it expects a monetisation event in fiscal 2026 (which ends 31 October).
